docs.title: Methane Alert and Response System Matched Filters retrievals for EMIT, PRISMA and EnMAP
docs.text: This repository provides an implementation with georeader of the matched filters methods of Roger et al. 2024 for EMIT, PRISMA and EnMAP. It also includes an adaptation of mag1c of Foote et al. 2020 for EMIT.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install marshsi

docs.text:

  • PRISMA example 👉 prisma_example.ipynb
  • EnMAP example 👉 enmap_example.ipynb

import os
import warnings
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# mag1c and georeader call np.divide/np.log with where= and no out=; the result is masked afterwards.
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message="'where' used without 'out'")

EMIT_FILENAMES = {
    "001": "../tests/data/EMIT_L1B_RAD_001_20220827T060753_2223904_013.nc",
    "002": "../tests/data/EMIT_L1B_RAD_002_20220827T060753.nc",
}
EMIT_VERSION = "002"
EMIT_FILENAME = EMIT_FILENAMES[EMIT_VERSION]

NEED_DOWNLOAD = not os.path.exists(EMIT_FILENAME)
print(f"File '{EMIT_FILENAME}' exists: {not NEED_DOWNLOAD}")

File '../tests/data/EMIT_L1B_RAD_002_20220827T060753.nc' exists: True


import georeader
from georeader.readers import emit, download_utils
from georeader import plot

# NASA's data archive requires creating an account for downloading EMIT files directly.
# Create a user and a token at the NASA Earthdata portal (https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov/profile)
# and set it as the EARTHDATA_TOKEN environment variable (or a GitHub Actions secret).
earthdata_nasa_account = True

if earthdata_nasa_account:
    # Also used by EMITImage to download the OBS file next to the radiance file.
    emit.AUTH_METHOD = "token"
    emit.TOKEN = os.environ.get("EARTHDATA_TOKEN", "")  # NASA Earthdata bearer token


def download_emit(filename):
    if earthdata_nasa_account:
        link = emit.get_radiance_link(filename)
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {emit.TOKEN}"}
        download_utils.download_product(link, headers=headers, verify=True, filename=filename)
    elif filename == EMIT_FILENAMES["001"]:
        # alternatively for the sake of this demo, we also uploaded the v001 scene (RAD and OBS) on our gdrive
        import subprocess
        out_dir = os.path.dirname(filename) + "/"
        subprocess.run(["gdown", "1jyFejO80Q82qUZ5tRPaDTqsBHefuXYa0", "-O", out_dir], check=True)
        subprocess.run(["gdown", "1a9k2YZDXfa4g95KlqCcKfkYcaA-QegYU", "-O", out_dir], check=True)
    else:
        raise ValueError("Only the v001 scene is on gdrive; download v002 with a NASA Earthdata token")


if NEED_DOWNLOAD:
    download_emit(EMIT_FILENAME)
else:
    print(f"Skipping download, '{EMIT_FILENAME}' already exists")

Skipping download, '../tests/data/EMIT_L1B_RAD_002_20220827T060753.nc' already exists


# cache_radiance=True keeps the full-spectrum windowed radiance in RAM after
# the first load_raw() call. The four downstream reads (mag1c, AT_MF_total_EMIT,
# load_rgb after to_crs, and plume_vetting.compute_emit) then all serve from
# the in-memory array instead of re-decompressing the ~1.85 GB file each time.
# The cache propagates through to_crs / read_from_bands clones by reference,
# so emit_image_utm built below shares it with rst.
rst = emit.EMITImage(EMIT_FILENAME, cache_radiance=True)

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from georeader.geotensor import GeoTensor
from marshsi.quantification import ATMOSPHERE_HEIGHT_METHANE
from marshsi import plume_vetting

from importlib import reload
reload(plume_vetting)

PLUMES_FILE = "../tests/data/plume_vetting/plumes_emit.gpkg"
plumes_gdf = gpd.read_file(PLUMES_FILE)
polygons = [geom.geoms[0] for geom in plumes_gdf.geometry]

# Convert WMF from ppm → ppm·m (multiply by effective column height in metres)
wmf_values = wmf_geo.values

docs.title: EMIT product versions
docs.text:
NASA's LP DAAC ended forward processing of the EMIT v001 products on 2026-08-31 (EMIT Version 1 and Existing Version 2 Forward Processing Ended). New acquisitions are published as L1B radiance v002, with the L2A mask as a separate v003 product (EMIT Version 2 Level 1B and Level 2A, and Version 3 Level 2A Data Products Released). Older acquisitions are being reprocessed to v002.

v002 product names drop the orbit and scene numbers (EMIT_L1B_RAD_002_20220827T060753 instead of EMIT_L1B_RAD_001_20220827T060753_2223904_013), and reading them requires georeader 2.4 or later. The marshsi retrievals work on both versions. This notebook runs on v002 by default (EMIT_VERSION below), and the last section repeats the demo on v001 of the same acquisition and compares the two.

docs.title: Plume vetting
docs.text:
Plume vetting is a spectral validation step that checks whether the pixels inside each detected plume actually show the CH₄ absorption signature relative to nearby background pixels. The method is described in:

> C. Xiang, D. R. Thompson, R. O. Green, J. E. Fahlen, A. K. Thorpe, P. G. Brodrick, > R. W. Coleman, A. M. Lopez, and C. D. Elder, Identification of false methane plumes > for orbital imaging spectrometers: A case study with EMIT, > Remote Sensing of Environment, 2025. >

docs.title: Same demo on EMIT v001
docs.text: The cells below repeat the retrievals and the plume vetting on the other product version of the same acquisition, and compare both versions. The two versions are georeferenced to the same UTM zone but not to the same grid, because the v002 geolocation differs slightly from v001.

# Azure credentials for the UNEP IMEO container. Set these as environment
# variables (or GitHub Actions secrets) so the integration tests can download
# the data in CI; leave them unset to use a file already in tests/data/.
SAS_TOKEN = os.environ.get("SAS_TOKEN", "")
AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT = os.environ.get("AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT", "")
CONTAINER = os.environ.get("CONTAINER_NAME", "")

folder_dest = "../tests/data/PRISMA"
tile = "PRS_L1_STD_OFFL_20250316071846_20250316071850_0001"
path_raster_dst = os.path.join(folder_dest, f"{tile}.he5")

NEED_DOWNLOAD = not os.path.exists(path_raster_dst)
print(f"File '{path_raster_dst}' exists: {not NEED_DOWNLOAD}")

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from georeader.geotensor import GeoTensor
from marshsi.quantification import ATMOSPHERE_HEIGHT_METHANE
from marshsi.plume_vetting import compute_prisma, plot_vetting

PLUMES_FILE = "../tests/data/plume_vetting/plumes_prisma.gpkg"
plumes_gdf = gpd.read_file(PLUMES_FILE)
polygons = [geom.geoms[0] for geom in plumes_gdf.geometry]

# Convert WMF from ppm → ppm·m (multiply by effective column height in metres)
wmf_values = wmf.values
if wmf_values.ndim == 3:
    wmf_values = wmf_values[0]
wmf_arr = np.where(
    wmf_values == wmf.fill_value_default,
    wmf.fill_value_default,
    wmf_values * ATMOSPHERE_HEIGHT_METHANE,
)
wmf_arr = np.where(~np.isfinite(wmf_arr), wmf.fill_value_default, wmf_arr)

wmf_ppmxm = GeoTensor(wmf_arr, transform=wmf.transform, crs=wmf.crs,
                      fill_value_default=wmf.fill_value_default)

results = compute_prisma(
    pi=rst,
    cmf=wmf_ppmxm,
    polygons=polygons,
    min_polygon_size=20,
    random_seed=42,
)

summary = (
    pd.DataFrame.from_dict(results, orient="index")
    .reindex(columns=["D_norm", "alpha_con_len"])
    .rename_axis("polygon")
    .sort_index()
)

docs.text:
Author: Gonzalo Mateo-García

See example of using PRISMA reader in georeader.

The Window-Wide Matched Filter is proposed in: > J. Roger, L. Guanter, J. Gorroño, and I. Irakulis-Loitxate, “Exploiting the entire near-infrared spectral range to improve the detection of methane plumes with high-resolution imaging spectrometers,” Atmospheric Measurement Techniques, vol. 17, no. 4, pp. 1333–1346, Feb. 2024, doi: 10.5194/amt-17-1333-2024.

docs.title: Plume vetting
docs.text:
Plume vetting is a spectral validation step that checks whether the pixels inside each detected plume actually show the CH₄ absorption signature relative to nearby background pixels.

The method is described in:

> C. Xiang, D. R. Thompson, R. O. Green, J. E. Fahlen, A. K. Thorpe, P. G. Brodrick, > R. W. Coleman, A. M. Lopez, and C. D. Elder, Identification of false methane plumes > for orbital imaging spectrometers: A case study with EMIT, > Remote Sensing of Environment, 2025. >
